question.text: STCG on listed equity shares (holding < 12 months) post July 2024 is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Listed equity shares held for 12 months or less are short-term capital assets. Following the July 2024 Budget, the short-term capital gains rate on such equity (Section 111A) was increased to 20% from the earlier 15%. The Trap: 15% was the rate prevailing before July 2024 and no longer applies; 'slab rate' applies to other short-term gains (e.g. unlisted shares, debt funds) but not to listed equity STCG covered by Section 111A; 'zero' is incorrect — listed equity STCG is taxable. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-B workbook (pp. 185-186) supports that listed securities held 12 months or less are short-term capital assets, but does not state the 20% post-July-2024 STCG rate or the July 2024 rate change in the pages checked. The rate framing above reflects the current Income Tax Act position rather than a workbook quote.
